newsitem.title: UK: Stg strength a dilemma for policy-BOE's George.
newsitem.headline: Stg strength a dilemma for policy-BOE's George.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George repeated his assertion that sterling's strength gave rise to a "genuine dilemma" for monetary policy.
In the Bank's annual report, George said the effect of the pound on the tradeable sectors of the economy could not be ignored.
"But nor can we expose the whole of the rest of the economy to significant inflationary risks which would then need to be addressed by a more abrupt tightening of policy at a later stage," he said.

George said some of the influences on the pound, such as the fact that Britain was at a more advanced stage in the economic cycle than much of Europe and market uncertainties about a single currency, "are likely to reverse in time."
"But in the meantime, they give rise to a genuine dilemma in the sense that there is no ideal short-run solution," George said.
In a foreword to the annual report, George said he welcomed Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's decision to give the Bank responsibility for setting interest rates.
"We think that will strengthen the process and make it more likely that we can, over time, achieve the stable economic growth which is the ultimate objective," he said.
Inflation had averaged around 2-3/4 percent over the last four years.
"That is not as low as it needs to be if we are to eliminate inflationary expectations, but it is nevertheless lower, and has persisted for longer, than we have seen in a generation."
On a single European currency, George said the Bank's sympathy lay with those who emphasised the importance of sustainable convergence rather than the timetable for the start of EMU.
"Nevertheless, our planning assumption is that the euro will go ahead on time, at least among a core group of countries," George added.
